Welcome
Embrace Opportunities - Choose Kindness - Value Everyone
................................................................................
Welcome to Westonzoyland Primary School!
It is a true pleasure to address you as the Headteacher of Westonzoyland Community Primary School. I would like to take this opportunity on behalf of our whole school community to welcome you to our school and our website.
As a primary school, we are very aware that we are helping to create the citizens of the future, and at Westonzoyland, we are really proud of our children: we seek to do the best for them in everything we do. Through our engaging curriculum and learning environment we build children’s enthusiasm and wonder for learning. We strive to provide opportunities and experiences outside of the classroom that develop collaborative and team-building skills, enabling our children to be well-rounded individuals. Health and wellbeing is fundamental to our values and to our aims of providing an excellent, all-round education. Our PE curriculum and after-school provision provide opportunities aplenty for children to learn about the importance of staying physically fit, of enjoying exercise, and how to look after their well-being.
At Westonzoyland, we are a friendly, caring school with high expectations for all our pupils. Our wonderful staff are dedicated to the children they teach and to making Westonzoyland the best school it can be. We are so lucky to have great support from our community and our governors, which enables us to be constantly changing and improving.
We hope that this site helps you to learn all about our school, however, if you have any further questions then please don't hesitate to get in touch with us. Visits are encouraged and welcomed: I would be delighted to show you around our wonderful school.

PE and Sport Premium
At Westonzoyland we believe that physical activity is of vital importance, not only to developing healthy bodies but also healthy minds.
We promote physical activity through our PE lessons, delivered mainly by our PE teachers, Mrs Williams and Mr Hudson. Weekly outdoor learning sessions also enable our children to be physically active, as does our after-school activity club provision, which is mostly led by our passionate staff; providing further opportunities to enrich our 'PE offer' to the children.
Our PE curriculum is threaded through our science, DT and RSHE learning. We focus on the development of physical, social and health knowledge and skills. Yoga is also taught throughout the school by Miss Hellier, our specialist Yoga teacher. As well as the physical benefits of Yoga, the children complete mindfulness activities and learn how to regulate their bodies, and achieve a sense of calm.
Please read the information below which gives details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.

Home Reading
Reading at home is the most vital of all homework activities. Evidence suggests that children who read for enjoyment every day not only perform better in reading tests than those who don’t, but also develop a broader vocabulary, increased general knowledge and a better understanding of other cultures.
In fact, reading for pleasure is more likely to determine whether a child does well at school than their social or economic background.
At our school all children MUST read at least 5 times per week (Monday - Friday) for a period of no less than 15 minutes. We consider reading at home every day to be best practice and encourage parents to liaise with their child's class teacher should they have any constraints with supporting reading at home.

Our Governors
Strategic Plan 2023 - 2025
Welcome to our Governors' section.
The Governing Body brings to the school and its children a variety of skills and interests. Governors usually serve a four year term (and can be re-elected or appointed for a new term of office).
The role of the Governing Body is to ensure that our school provides an effective education for our children and meets all the statutory requirements. This is a huge task and our governors are committed and hard working. In particular the governing body seeks to ensure:
Our school Governing Body meets twice each term and most Governors also have additional roles to focus on for example Safeguarding, Health and Safety and Special Educational Needs and Disability. In between meetings Governors may also visit the school to observe different aspects of life at school. Our School Improvement Plan guides the work of the Governing Body and a small group of Governors has strategic oversight of each priority.
The Chair of Governors
The role of Chair of Governors is shared between two co-chairs, Amy Saturley and Laura Proud. They share the chairing of Governors' meetings and both have regular meetings with the Headteacher. Although the role is carried out by two people, both individuals have the authority to carry out the role and responsibilities of the Chair of Governors.
Amy Saturley is the lead co-chair, that is the first point of contact for the headteacher, parents, the local authority, the Department for Education (DfE) and other stakeholders.

My career for the last 25 years has been in finance and welfare in a variety of different roles. Westonzoyland is a wonderful village and I believe the school and the children are central to its future success.

Curriculum
Information about our curriculum:
Curriculum Statement: Westonzoyland Community Primary School
At Westonzoyland Community Primary School, the curriculum is central to all that we do. Our curriculum is purposeful, ambitious and relevant to our children and their lives. We aim to engage children in enjoyable learning experiences which enable them to develop the knowledge, skills and attitudes they need to succeed in a rapidly changing world. We seek to instil a lifelong love of learning that motivates every child to flourish academically, socially and personally.
The curriculum at Westonzoyland Community Primary School provides a broad, balanced and enriched education, placing a high importance on English, including reading, grammar and oracy, mathematics and an understanding of the wider world and our local community. We value creativity and are proud to provide opportunities through our wider curriculum for children to experience specialist music and art teaching, as well as participation in our year-round Forest School programme. These opportunities enable children to learn new skills, develop resilience, work collaboratively and discover their own talents and interests.
In line with the Education Inspection Framework (Ofsted, 2025a), our approach is organised around three key elements:
How the curriculum is taught.
The outcomes pupils attain and the progress they make.
Inclusion underpins all aspects of our work. We strive to ensure that all pupils, including disadvantaged pupils, pupils with SEND and those who face barriers to learning, have full access to an ambitious curriculum that enables them to achieve well and prepare successfully for the next stage of their education.
Curriculum: What is taught
Ofsted's Curriculum Expectations
School leaders and staff design, adopt and adapt a high-quality, ambitious, broad and balanced curriculum for all pupils, paying particular regard to disadvantaged pupils, those with SEND and pupils who may face additional barriers to their learning or wellbeing.
At Westonzoyland Community Primary School, we intend to provide an ambitious, broad, balanced and creative curriculum that enables all groups of pupils to achieve as well as they can in both their academic and personal development.
Our curriculum aims:
We place particular emphasis on English, Mathematics, Computing, Science, Sport and the Performing Arts. Music, PE and Art benefit from specialist teaching.
Using the National Curriculum as our starting point, our curriculum is carefully planned and logically sequenced to ensure progression in knowledge and skills. We have developed clear progression maps to support teaching in our mixed-age classes and ensure consistency across year groups.
The curriculum at Westonzoyland offers a traditional, creative and inspiring educational experience that reflects our local community while preparing children to participate confidently in the wider world. Learning is designed to be meaningful, engaging and relevant, with appropriate connections made across subjects.
Different Types of Knowledge
Our curriculum planning incorporates different forms of knowledge:
Substantive knowledge – established facts and information.
Disciplinary knowledge – the methods and ways of thinking used within individual subjects.
Conceptual knowledge – important ideas and concepts pupils need to understand.
Procedural knowledge – the skills and techniques pupils need to apply.
The planning of the Early Years curriculum takes full account of the Statutory Framework for the Early Years Foundation Stage and Development Matters guidance. The curriculum covers all seven areas of learning and development and provides a strong foundation for future success.
Reading is Essential to Learning
Reading is a high priority throughout the school.
We use Twinkl Phonics, a DfE-validated phonics programme, to provide a structured and systematic approach to early reading and writing. Reading books are carefully matched to children's phonic knowledge, ensuring fluency, accuracy and confidence develop progressively.
"Reading is at the heart of our curriculum."
Andy Clark, Headteacher
Hamilton Brookes forms the basis of our mathematics curriculum planning. The scheme meets National Curriculum requirements and is well suited to our mixed-age classes. It supports the development of fluency, reasoning and problem-solving whilst maintaining a strong focus on arithmetic and mathematical confidence.
Pupils are provided with regular opportunities to apply literacy and numeracy skills across the curriculum.
The school follows Somerset's agreed RE syllabus, Awareness, Mystery and Value, which provides comprehensive long-term planning, progression and assessment opportunities from EYFS to Year 6.
The wider curriculum is informed by the Kapow curriculum framework. Subject-specific knowledge and skills are carefully planned to ensure progression and depth of understanding. Children learn not only knowledge but also how knowledge is generated and applied within each discipline.
Curriculum Enrichment
Our curriculum is enriched through educational visits, visitors, Forest School experiences, residential opportunities, clubs, performances and participation in community events.
Levels of Curriculum Planning
Our curriculum is organised through:
Attitudes, Learning Behaviours and Values
Through our curriculum and ethos, we actively promote:
Fundamental British Values
We seek to provide pupils with the experiences, knowledge and understanding needed to become successful and responsible citizens in modern Britain and the wider world.
We use the Kapow PSHE programme alongside our "No Outsiders" approach to foster wellbeing, inclusion, diversity and positive relationships.
Teaching: How Our Curriculum is Taught
High-quality teaching is the key to successful curriculum delivery and achievement.
At Westonzoyland Community Primary School, teachers have secure subject knowledge and high expectations for all learners. Professional development ensures staff remain informed about educational research, curriculum developments and effective practice.
Reading continues to be prioritised so that all pupils can access the full curriculum.
Teaching assistants are well trained and make valuable contributions to learning by supporting pupils effectively whilst promoting independence.
Assessment is used effectively to:
Learning environments are attractive, stimulating and purposeful. Displays celebrate achievement and support learning through the use of key vocabulary, knowledge and examples of high-quality work.
Achievement: The Outcomes for Pupils
Achievement encompasses both attainment and progress.
Through our ambitious curriculum and strong teaching, pupils develop secure knowledge, understanding and skills across the curriculum. Successful learning is reflected in the quality of work produced, classroom discussions, assessment outcomes and pupils' readiness for their next stage of education.
We want all pupils to:
Disadvantaged pupils and those with SEND are fully included in all aspects of school life. Through high-quality teaching, carefully considered adaptations and targeted support, pupils receive the help they need to achieve success.
We are confident that our pupils leave Westonzoyland Community Primary School equipped with the knowledge, skills, values and attitudes needed to thrive in secondary education and beyond.
Ofsted's Expectations for Achievement
Schools should provide a high-quality education so that all pupils, particularly disadvantaged pupils, pupils with SEND and those who face barriers to learning, achieve well and gain the knowledge and skills needed for future success.
At Westonzoyland Community Primary School, we are committed to ensuring that all pupils know more, remember more and are able to do more as a result of the education they receive. This achievement prepares them well for lifelong learning and active participation in modern society.

Pre-School
Welcome to Westonzoyland Pre-School!
Westonzoyland Pre-School (Fledglings) and Reception Class (Merlin) work together closely and alongside each other to ensure children are happy, secure and make good progress in their learning and development. We benefit from a large indoor learning environment that has a wide range of activities for the children to independently access and explore. Our large outdoor area is resourced with a splendid variety of activities for the children to explore and to learn about the natural world. Children’s interests are identified and discussed with parents/carers and incorporated into the planning and learning environment to enable the children to reach their full potential. Our dedicated staff team are very experienced and committed to supporting children and their families while they progress on their learning journey. All Staff in Pre-School are qualified in Early Years and Paediatric First Aid; other qualifications and training include Exploring Emotional Experiences, Somerset Total Communication (STC), Food Safety, Maths Garden, Mud Kitchen experiences, E-Safety, Phonics training, Supporting Positive Behaviours, Mastery of Mathematics and Moving and Handling.
Safeguarding Children
We benefit from good links with the school SENCo, Children’s Centres, local Health Visitor and other professionals. All staff have attended training about Safeguarding Children and Prevent Duty. We work with children, parents and other professionals to ensure the rights and safety of the children in our care.
Diversity and Equality We promote equality of opportunity, valuing diversity for all children and their families.
Our Pre-school DSL is Danni King.
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
We provide an environment in which all children are supported to reach their full potential. We work together to ensure our provision meets the needs of an individual child.
The transitions for Fledglings when they progress into the Merlin class is seamless, with the Reception teacher having formed good relationships with both child and parents prior to them starting school. Please call into school to pick up a welcome pack or call to arrange a visit to meet our friendly staff, gather more information and for you and your child to feel the experience of our enabling environment.
Fledglings – Mrs King (Pre-School)

Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium funding is an annual allocation of funds from the Government given to schools across the country. Each school’s funding allocation is calculated according to the number of pupils at the school who have been registered as eligible for ‘free school meals’ (FSM) in the last six years and for children who are ‘Looked After’ (CLA) for more than six months.
These funds are used to provide additional support and intervention for all students, but with a particular focus on those in receipt of FSM and those who are CLA. A key area where these funds are targeted is to ensure the continued personal, social and emotional progress of children as well as academic achievement.
If you think that you may qualify, please either ask for a form in the school office, or apply directly on the Somerset County Council website using this link: http://www.somerset.gov.uk/education-learning-and-schools/school-life/free-school-meals/
